data.cultural_impact: The name Rudratej is derived from two Sanskrit words – Rudra and Tej. Rudra is a name of lord Shiva, one of the primary deities in Hinduism. Tej refers to power, strength, and energy. Thus, the name Rudratej signifies a powerful ruler or lord associated with Lord Shiva.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Rudratej holds spiritual significance as it represents the divine power and rulership associated with Lord Shiva and Lord Vishwakarma. Lord Shiva, as Rudratej, is considered the source of cosmic power and supreme consciousness, the embodiment of creation, preservation, and destruction.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Rudratej: One who is ruled by Rudra, the god of destruction and transformation. It represents the individual's surrender to the forces of change and the divine will, inviting transformation and renewal.

historical_references.reference: Rudra, the god of primordial violence in Hinduism, is also known as Rudratej. In the Vedic period (1500-500 BCE), Rudra was depicted as a fierce, dark-skinned god, worshipped for protection and destruction.
historical_references.context: Depiction of Rudra as a deity

historical_references.reference: Later, in the Puranic period (500-1000 CE), Rudratej came to be identified with the god Shiva. During this time, Rudratej was revered as the lord of mountains and the god of the rivers, particularly the Saraswati.
historical_references.context: Identification of Rudratej with Shiva and his roles
